input.question: How was German culture effected by the years between the end of WWII and reunification?
input.ground_truth: I'm not a historian, but a German. So in fact there were two countries, DDR and BRD, or East Germany and West Germany. But in both countries the people were mostly german and spoke german. So there was no big cultural difference, except maybe food. Regarding patriotism: There was just a minority of people who were against a unification of the DDR and the BRD. The people were smart enough to see that the communist part of the world was crumbling and they wanted to be free. After the unification background checks of the administrative elite were executed. So you didn't really have supporters of the old regime in important positions anymore. I don't know if this answers your questions.

Okay! Imagine Germany was like a big family that got split into two parts after a big fight (World War II). One part was in the west and got lots of help to rebuild, and people there started listening to new music, wearing different clothes, and thinking new ideas. The other part was in the east and was controlled by a different group (the Soviets), so people there had fewer toys, different food, and had to follow stricter rules. 

For a long time, the two parts couldn’t talk to each other much. The people in the east grew up with different stories and games than the people in the west. When the wall came down and the two parts joined again (reunification), it was like the family got back together but didn’t know all the same games or songs anymore. 

So, German culture changed a lot because for a long time, the two sides lived very different lives. When they came back together, they had to learn from each other and mix their old and new ways of doing things.
